problem: Egocentric step-by-step VLN suffers from compounding errors, weak global spatial modeling and costly repeated action prediction. Existing map-based VLN methods still rely on incrementally updated memory graphs or scoring discrete path proposals, which limits continuous spatial reasoning.
motivation: Robots often already have pre-built maps from SLAM pre-exploration, so a full top-down map could be used for global planning. Predicting a full path in one pass avoids error accumulation and the per-step decision cost.
key_idea: Reformulate VLN as one-step global path planning on pre-built multi-modal top-down maps (TD-VLN), where a ViT-based network predicts dense path and goal probability maps in a single forward pass, followed by A* extraction.
insight: Adding Full Attention Residuals and then spatial-aware depth queries to the ViT mainly improves generalization to unseen layouts: Val Unseen SR goes 0.40 -> 0.44 -> 0.47 while Val Seen SR drops from 0.63 to 0.57, so the seen-unseen gap shrinks from 23pp to 10pp. Modality ablation shows RGB-only (0.20 unseen SR) and semantic-only (0.43) are both worse than the full RGB+occupancy+semantic fusion (0.47). Noise-augmented training makes the model robust to map degradation.
method: Top-Down Map Fuser: concatenates RGB (3ch), binary occupancy (1ch) and a learnable 8-dim embedding of the 41-class semantic map into a 12-channel input tensor.

Multi-modal fusion: ViT patch tokens (16x16 patches, 256x256 input) get start position and quaternion rotation embeddings added, then 12 stacked cross-attention layers query frozen BERT instruction features.

ViT encoder with Attention Residuals: 12-layer Pre-LN ViT using Full Attention Residuals (depth-wise softmax mixing of all earlier layer outputs), with per-token spatial-aware depth query q = w_l + f(e_n), zero-initialized.
Decoder: progressive stride-2 transposed convolutions (768->256->128->64->32) plus a final 3x3 conv give 2-channel path and goal probability maps at 256x256.

Path Extractor: goal = argmax of the goal map; cost = 1/(P_path+eps) on free cells and 1000 on obstacles; 8-connected A* from the start; snaps to the nearest reachable cell if the goal is unreachable.
Loss: BCE on path and goal maps (alpha=5) plus continuity regularizers (Sobel gradient smoothness, start-anchor MSE, erosion-based fragmentation penalty; lambda=0.1).
R2R-TopDown dataset: R2R-CE single-floor episodes projected onto MP3D top-down RGB/occupancy/semantic maps built in Habitat by frontier exploration with GT poses.

setting.backbone: ViT-B/16 with cross-attention and Attention Residuals + frozen BERT-base-uncased (trained from scratch apart from BERT), A* post-processing
setting.training_data: R2R-TopDown train: 6,196 single-floor R2R-CE episodes on MP3D top-down maps; 400 epochs with rotation/translation/color-jitter augmentation
setting.observation: Global pre-built top-down maps (RGB, occupancy, semantic 41 classes) + instruction + start position and quaternion rotation
setting.action_space: Complete 2D path on the map (pixel waypoints via A*), converted to metric waypoints for a local controller
setting.simulator: Habitat (MP3D scenes) for dataset and map construction
setting.privileged: Pre-built full top-down maps, built with simulator GT poses and MP3D GT semantic annotations (semantic labels from MP3D 41 classes, occupancy derived from the floor class); GT start pose

numbers_note: Results are on the authors' own R2R-TopDown filtered split (single-floor only), not the standard R2R/R2R-CE benchmark. Baseline numbers from other papers are on full R2R val-unseen, so they are not directly comparable. Robustness and modality ablations are in appendix tables (e.g., noise-aug SR 0.483 on clean Val Unseen).
results: NavOne (AR-Full+SQ) reaches Val Unseen SR 0.47 / SPL 0.43, above IPPD (0.45/0.42 on full R2R, 0.37/0.31 re-evaluated on the filtered set), MapNav (0.40) and WS-MGMap (0.39). Planning takes 37 ms per episode, 8x faster than IPPD (300 ms) and ~80x faster than ETPNav (2970 ms). MapNav keeps a lower NE (4.93).
limitations: Requires a pre-built, accurate top-down map; assumes a static environment and cannot handle dynamic obstacles or online updates.

Evaluated only on a filtered single-floor R2R-TopDown split; no multi-floor support, and comparisons with baselines are not on identical episodes. The 41-class semantic vocabulary misses fine-grained objects referenced in instructions.

Maps and semantics used in evaluation come from simulator GT poses and MP3D annotations; real-robot results are only qualitative, and performance degrades under heavy map noise unless noise augmentation is used.
